introduction.en: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services. It is broadly categorized into demand-pull and cost-push based on its origin.
introduction.hi: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services. It is broadly categorized into demand-pull and cost-push based on its origin.

body.en: Demand-pull inflation occurs when aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply, often due to excess money supply. The RBI manages this by increasing the Repo Rate to reduce liquidity. Cost-push inflation arises from rising production costs, such as oil prices or wages. The RBI has limited control over cost-push inflation, which requires supply-side fiscal interventions by the government.

Cost-push inflation arises from rising production costs, such as oil prices or wages. conclusion.en: Effective inflation management requires a synergy between the RBI's monetary policy and the government's fiscal and supply-side policies.
